Transforms run in command-line order, so rotations given before this option are respected. --orient 1 runs after all transforms and replaces the orientation.

gyroid_optimized.label: Z-buckling bias optimization (experimental)
gyroid_optimized.tooltip: Tightens the gyroid wave along the Z (vertical) axis at low infill density to shorten the effective vertical column length and improve Z-axis compression buckling resistance. Filament use is preserved. No effect at ~30% sparse infill density and above. Only applies when Sparse infill pattern is set to Gyroid.

has_filament_switcher.label: Has filament switcher
has_filament_switcher.tooltip: Printer has a filament switcher hardware (e.g., AMS).

has_single_extruder_multi_material_primi.label: Has single extruder MM priming
has_single_extruder_multi_material_primi.tooltip: Are the extra multi-material priming regions used in this print?

has_wipe_tower.label: Has wipe tower
has_wipe_tower.tooltip: Whether or not wipe tower is being generated in the print.

help_fff.label: Help (FFF options)
help_fff.tooltip: Show the full list of print/G-code configuration options.

help_sla.label: Help (SLA options)
help_sla.tooltip: Show the full list of SLA print configuration options.

high_current_on_filament_swap.label: High extruder current on filament swap
high_current_on_filament_swap.tooltip: It may be beneficial to increase the extruder motor current during the filament exchange sequence to allow for rapid ramming feed rates and to overcome resistance when loading a filament with an ugly shaped tip.

high_precision_gcode.label: High precision G-code (experimental)
high_precision_gcode.tooltip:
Write X, Y, Z, I and J with 4 decimal places instead of 3, and E with 6 instead of 5, to reduce rounding errors in the G-code. With relative E distances, the rounding error of each move is also carried over to the next one. Supports are removed after printing, so they keep the standard precision. This may help stabilize extrusion with small nozzles (e.g. 0.2 mm) and thin layers (e.g. 0.08 mm or less), where each move extrudes so little material that rounding errors matter most. The effect depends strongly on how well the rest of the settings are tuned and may be hard to notice unless the print profile is well calibrated.

The G-code file becomes about 10 percent larger, which may slow down printers that parse G-code slowly.

hole_to_polyhole.label: Convert holes to polyholes
hole_to_polyhole.tooltip:
Search for almost-circular holes that span more than one layer and convert the geometry to polyholes. Use the nozzle size and the (biggest) diameter to compute the polyhole.
See http://hydraraptor.blogspot.com/2011/02/polyholes.html

hole_to_polyhole_max_edges.label: Maximum Polyhole edge count
hole_to_polyhole_max_edges.tooltip:
Maximum number of polyhole edges
This setting limits the amount of edges a polyhole can have

hole_to_polyhole_threshold.label: Polyhole detection margin
hole_to_polyhole_threshold.tooltip:
Maximum defection of a point to the estimated radius of the circle.
As cylinders are often exported as triangles of varying size, points may not be on the circle circumference. This setting allows you some leeway to broaden the detection.
In mm or in % of the radius.

host_type.label: Host Type
host_type.tooltip: Orca Slicer can upload G-code files to a printer host. This field must contain the kind of the host.

hot_plate_temp.label: Other layers
hot_plate_temp.tooltip: This is the bed temperature for layers except for the first one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the High Temp Plate.

hot_plate_temp_initial_layer.label: First layer
hot_plate_temp_initial_layer.tooltip: This is the bed temperature of the first layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the High Temp Plate.

idle_temperature.label: Idle temperature
idle_temperature.tooltip: Nozzle temperature when the tool is currently not used in multi-tool setups. This is only used when 'Ooze prevention' is active in Print Settings. Set to 0 to disable.

ignore_nonexistent_config.label: Ignore non-existent config files
ignore_nonexistent_config.tooltip: Do not fail if a file supplied to --load does not exist.

imex_carriage_margin.label: Safety Margin
imex_carriage_margin.tooltip: Non-blocking advisory clearance strip (mm) drawn inside the primary zone at each carriage boundary. Parts placed within this strip will still slice; it is a visual reminder to leave extra clearance near the zone edge.

imex_firmware_managed_zones.label: Firmware-managed zones
imex_firmware_managed_zones.tooltip: When enabled, the slicer emits G-code with the primary zone's contents centered on bed origin (0,0). The printer firmware is responsible for placing copies/mirrors at each physical zone position. Enable only on printers whose firmware applies its own zone offsets in copy/mirror mode (e.g. RepRapFirmware IDEX duplication mode). Has no effect in Primary mode.

imex_gantry_count.label: Gantry Count
imex_gantry_count.tooltip: Number of independent Y-axis gantries. 1 for IDEX/single-rail IQEX. 2 for dual-gantry systems (divides bed into rows).

imex_head_filament_map.label: IDEX/IQEX head filament map
imex_head_filament_map.tooltip: Per-plate override mapping physical heads to filament slots (1-based). Empty means each head uses the first filament that the printer's physical extruder map routes to it.

imex_mode_active_tools.label: IDEX/IQEX Mode Active Tools
imex_mode_active_tools.tooltip: Tool role assignments for each mode. Format: "idx:P,idx:C,idx:M" where P=Primary, C=Copy, M=Mirror (e.g. "0:P,1:C,2:M,3:M"). Managed by the IDEX/IQEX Modes editor in the Printer preset.

imex_mode_gcodes.label: IDEX/IQEX Mode G-codes
imex_mode_gcodes.tooltip: G-code or macro call to inject at print start for each mode.

imex_mode_names.label: IDEX/IQEX Mode Names
imex_mode_names.tooltip: Display names for each user-defined IDEX/IQEX parallel print mode.

imex_nozzle_clearance_x.label: Nozzle Clearance X
imex_nozzle_clearance_x.tooltip: Distance (mm) from the nozzle to the collision-side carriage edge in X. Used to calculate the width of the collision exclusion strip at each X boundary.

imex_nozzle_clearance_y.label: Nozzle Clearance Y
imex_nozzle_clearance_y.tooltip: Distance (mm) from the nozzle to the collision-side carriage edge in Y. Used to calculate the width of the collision exclusion strip at each Y boundary.

imex_parallel_mode.label: IDEX/IQEX Print Mode
imex_parallel_mode.tooltip: Name of the active IDEX/IQEX parallel print mode, or "primary" for single-carriage printing. Requires IDEX/IQEX Printer enabled in the Printer preset (Printer \u2192 Multimaterial \u2192 IDEX/IQEX Configuration).

imex_tool_layout.label: Tool 0 Position
imex_tool_layout.tooltip: Physical position on the bed where tool T0 (index 0) is located. Determines how tool indices map to bed zones. For single-gantry setups (IDEX) only left/right matters; for dual-gantry setups (IQEX) all four corners are selectable (front = lower Y / near the operator, rear = higher Y / back of machine).

imex_tools_per_gantry.label: Tools per Gantry
imex_tools_per_gantry.tooltip: Number of independent toolheads per gantry along X. 2 for IDEX-style.

imex_viz_theme.label: Visualization Theme
imex_viz_theme.tooltip: Color theme for IDEX/IQEX bed zone visualization. Choose a colorblind-friendly theme if needed.

independent_support_layer_height.label: Independent support layer height
independent_support_layer_height.tooltip: Support layer uses layer height independent with object layer. This is to support customizing Z-gap and save print time. This option will be invalid when the prime tower is enabled.

infill_anchor.label: Sparse infill anchor length
infill_anchor.tooltip:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Orca Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to this parameter, but no longer than anchor_length_max.
Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring perimeters connected to a single infill line.

infill_anchor_max.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor
infill_anchor_max.tooltip:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Orca Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than this parameter is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to infill_anchor, but no longer than this parameter.
If set to 0, the old algorithm for infill connection will be used, it should create the same result as with 1000 & 0.

infill_combination.label: Infill combination
infill_combination.tooltip: Automatically combine sparse infill of several layers to print together in order to reduce time. Walls are still printed with original layer height.

infill_combination_max_layer_height.label: Infill combination - Max layer height
infill_combination_max_layer_height.tooltip:
Maximum layer height for the combined sparse infill.

Set it to 0 or 100% to use the nozzle diameter (for maximum reduction in print time) or a value of ~80% to maximize sparse infill strength.

The number of layers over which infill is combined is derived by dividing this value with the layer height and rounded down to the nearest decimal.

Use either absolute mm values (eg. 0.32mm for a 0.4mm nozzle) or % values (eg 80%). This value must not be larger than the nozzle diameter.

infill_complete_top.label: Fill pattern tops
infill_complete_top.tooltip: Choose this option if you want to completely fill in the tops of the infill pattern

infill_direction.label: Sparse infill direction
infill_direction.tooltip: This is the angle for sparse infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of lines.

infill_lock_depth.label: Infill lock depth
infill_lock_depth.tooltip: The parameter sets the overlapping depth between the interior and skin.

infill_overhang_angle.label: Infill overhang angle
infill_overhang_angle.tooltip: The angle of the infill angled lines. 60° will result in a pure honeycomb.

infill_shift_step.label: Infill shift step
infill_shift_step.tooltip: This parameter adds a slight displacement to each layer of infill to create a cross texture.

infill_wall_overlap.label: Infill/wall overlap
infill_wall_overlap.tooltip: This allows the infill area to be enlarged slightly to overlap with walls for better bonding. The percentage value is relative to the inner wall line width. Set this value to ~10-15% to minimize potential over extrusion and accumulation of material resulting in rough top surfaces.

initial_extruder.label: Initial extruder
initial_extruder.tooltip: Zero-based index of the first extruder used in the print. Same as initial_tool.

initial_layer_acceleration.label: First layer
initial_layer_acceleration.tooltip: This is the printing acceleration for the first layer. Using limited acceleration can improve build plate adhesion.

initial_layer_fan_speed.label: First layer fan speed
initial_layer_fan_speed.tooltip:
Sets an exact fan speed for the first layer, overriding all other cooling settings. Useful for protecting 3D-printed toolhead parts (e.g. Voron-style ABS/ASA ducts) from a hot bed. A small amount of airflow cools the ducts down, without using full cooling that may in certain conditions hurt first-layer adhesion.
From the second layer onwards, normal cooling resumes.
If "Full fan speed at layer" is also set, the fan ramps smoothly from this value on the first layer up to your target by the chosen layer.
Only available when "No cooling for the first" is 0.
Set to -1 to disable it.

initial_layer_infill_speed.label: First layer infill
initial_layer_infill_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for the first layer except for walls and brim, such as infill, gap fill and support.

initial_layer_line_width.label: First layer
initial_layer_line_width.tooltip: Line width of the first layer. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

initial_layer_min_bead_width.label: First layer minimum wall width
initial_layer_min_bead_width.tooltip: The minimum wall width that should be used for the first layer is recommended to be set to the same size as the nozzle. This adjustment is expected to enhance adhesion.

initial_layer_print_height.label: First layer height
initial_layer_print_height.tooltip: Height of the first layer. Making the first layer height thicker can improve build plate adhesion.

initial_layer_speed.label: First layer
initial_layer_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for the walls and brim of the first layer.

initial_layer_travel_acceleration.label: First layer travel
initial_layer_travel_acceleration.tooltip:
Travel acceleration of first layer.
The percentage value is relative to Travel Acceleration.

initial_layer_travel_jerk.label: First layer travel
initial_layer_travel_jerk.tooltip:
Travel jerk of first layer.
The percentage value is relative to Travel Jerk.

initial_layer_travel_speed.label: First layer travel speed
initial_layer_travel_speed.tooltip: Travel speed of the first layer.

initial_tool.label: Initial tool
initial_tool.tooltip: Zero-based index of the first extruder used in the print. Same as initial_extruder.

inner_wall_filament_id.label: Inner walls
inner_wall_filament_id.tooltip:
Filament to print inner walls.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

inner_wall_flow_ratio.label: Inner wall flow ratio
inner_wall_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for inner walls.

The actual inner wall flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

inner_wall_line_width.label: Inner wall
inner_wall_line_width.tooltip: Line width of inner wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

inner_wall_speed.label: Inner wall
inner_wall_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for inner walls.

input_filename_base.label: Input filename without extension
input_filename_base.tooltip: Source filename of the first object, without extension.

input_shaping_damp_x.label: XAxis
input_shaping_damp_x.tooltip:
Damping ratio for the X axis input shaper.
Zero will use the firmware damping ratio.
To disable input shaping, use the Disable type.
RRF: X and Y values are equal.

input_shaping_damp_y.label: YAxis
input_shaping_damp_y.tooltip:
Damping ratio for the Y axis input shaper.
Zero will use the firmware damping ratio.
To disable input shaping, use the Disable type.

input_shaping_emit.label: Emit input shaping
input_shaping_emit.tooltip:
Override firmware input shaping settings.
If disabled, firmware settings are used.

input_shaping_freq_x.label: XAxis
input_shaping_freq_x.tooltip:
Resonant frequency for the X axis input shaper.
Zero will use the firmware frequency.
To disable input shaping, use the Disable type.
RRF: X and Y values are equal.

input_shaping_freq_y.label: YAxis
input_shaping_freq_y.tooltip:
Resonant frequency for the Y axis input shaper.
Zero will use the firmware frequency.
To disable input shaping, use the Disable type.

input_shaping_type.label: Input shaper type
input_shaping_type.tooltip:
Choose the input shaper algorithm.
Default uses the firmware default settings.
Disable turns off input shaping in the firmware.

inspect_mesh.label: Inspect mesh (JSON to stdout)
inspect_mesh.tooltip: Print a JSON summary of each loaded object to stdout, then exit: its bounding boxes and the convex hull faces it can be laid on, with their normals, areas and centers. These are the faces the --ground-* options choose from. Machine-readable alternative to --info.

inspect_paint.label: Inspect paint (JSON to stdout)
inspect_paint.tooltip: Print a structured JSON summary of every painted layer (supports, seam, MMU color, fuzzy-skin) already stored on the loaded model \u2014 per-state facet count, surface area, and mesh-local bounding box \u2014 then exit. Machine-readable alternative to opening the paint gizmos in the GUI.

interface_shells.label: Interface shells
interface_shells.tooltip: Force the generation of solid shells between adjacent materials/volumes. Useful for multi-extruder prints with translucent materials or manual soluble support material.

interlocking_beam.label: Use beam interlocking
interlocking_beam.tooltip: Generate interlocking beam structure at the locations where different filaments touch. This improves the adhesion between filaments, especially models printed in different materials.

interlocking_beam_layer_count.label: Interlocking beam layers
interlocking_beam_layer_count.tooltip: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.

interlocking_beam_width.label: Interlocking beam width
interlocking_beam_width.tooltip: The width of the interlocking structure beams.

interlocking_boundary_avoidance.label: Interlocking boundary avoidance
interlocking_boundary_avoidance.tooltip: The distance from the outside of a model where interlocking structures will not be generated, measured in cells.

interlocking_depth.label: Interlocking depth
interlocking_depth.tooltip: The distance from the boundary between filaments to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.

internal_bridge_angle.label: Internal bridge infill direction
internal_bridge_angle.tooltip:
Internal Bridging angle override.
If left to zero, the bridging angle will be calculated automatically for each specific bridge.
Otherwise the provided angle will be used according to:
 - The absolute coordinates
 - The absolute coordinates + Model rotation: If Align directions to model is enabled
 - The optimal automatic angle + this value: If 'Relative Bridge Angle' is enabled

Use 180° for zero absolute angle.

internal_bridge_density.label: Internal bridge density
internal_bridge_density.tooltip:
Controls the density (spacing) of internal bridge lines.
Internal bridges act as intermediate support between sparse infill and top solid infill and can strongly affect top surface quality.

- Higher than 100% density (Recommended Max 125%):
  - Pros: Improves internal bridge strength and support under top layers, reducing sagging and improving top-surface finish.
  - Cons: Increases material use and print time; excessive density may cause overextrusion and internal stresses.

- Lower than 100% density (Min 10%):
  - Pros: Can reduce pillowing and improve cooling (more airflow through the bridge), and may speed up printing.
  - Cons: May reduce internal support, increasing the risk of sagging and top surface defects.

This option works particularly well when combined with the second internal bridge over infill option to improve bridging further before solid infill is extruded.

internal_bridge_fan_speed.label: Internal bridges fan speed
internal_bridge_fan_speed.tooltip:
The part cooling fan speed used for all internal bridges. Set to -1 to use the overhang fan speed settings instead.

Reducing the internal bridges fan speed, compared to your regular fan speed, can help reduce part warping due to excessive cooling applied over a large surface for a prolonged period of time.

internal_bridge_flow.label: Internal bridge flow ratio
internal_bridge_flow.tooltip:
This value governs the thickness of the internal bridge layer. This is the first layer over sparse infill so increasing it may increase strength and upper layer quality.
Values above 1.0: Increase the amount of material while maintaining line spacing. This can improve line contact and strength.
Values below 1.0: Reduce the amount of material while adjusting line spacing to maintain contact. This can improve sagging.

The actual bridge flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

internal_bridge_speed.label: Internal
internal_bridge_speed.tooltip: Speed of internal bridges. If the value is expressed as a percentage, it will be calculated based on the bridge_speed. Default value is 150%.

internal_solid_filament_id.label: Internal solid infill
internal_solid_filament_id.tooltip:
Filament to print internal solid infill.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

internal_solid_infill_acceleration.label: Internal solid infill
internal_solid_infill_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of internal solid infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.

internal_solid_infill_flow_ratio.label: Internal solid infill flow ratio
internal_solid_infill_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for internal solid infill.

The actual internal solid infill flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

internal_solid_infill_line_width.label: Internal solid infill
internal_solid_infill_line_width.tooltip: Line width of internal solid infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

internal_solid_infill_pattern.label: Internal solid infill pattern
internal_solid_infill_pattern.tooltip: Line pattern of internal solid infill. if the detect narrow internal solid infill be enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the small area.

internal_solid_infill_speed.label: Internal solid infill
internal_solid_infill_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for internal solid infill, not including the top or bottom surface.

ironing_angle.label: Ironing angle offset
ironing_angle.tooltip: The angle of ironing lines offset from the top surface.

ironing_angle_fixed.label: Fixed ironing angle
ironing_angle_fixed.tooltip: Use a fixed absolute angle for ironing.

ironing_expansion.label: Ironing expansion
ironing_expansion.tooltip: Expand or contract the ironing area.

ironing_fan_speed.label: Ironing fan speed
ironing_fan_speed.tooltip:
This part cooling fan speed is applied when ironing. Setting this parameter to a lower than regular speed reduces possible nozzle clogging due to the low volumetric flow rate, making the interface smoother.
Set to -1 to disable it.

ironing_flow.label: Ironing flow
ironing_flow.tooltip: This is the amount of material to be extruded during ironing. It is relative to the flow of normal layer height. Too high a value will result in overextrusion on the surface.

ironing_inset.label: Ironing inset
ironing_inset.tooltip: The distance to keep from the edges. A value of 0 sets this to half of the nozzle diameter.

ironing_pattern.label: Ironing Pattern
ironing_pattern.tooltip: The pattern that will be used when ironing.

ironing_spacing.label: Ironing line spacing
ironing_spacing.tooltip: This is the distance between the lines used for ironing.

ironing_speed.label: Ironing speed
ironing_speed.tooltip: This is the print speed for ironing lines.

ironing_type.label: Ironing type
ironing_type.tooltip: Ironing uses a small flow to print at the same height of a surface to make flat surfaces smoother. This setting controls which layers are being ironed.

is_extruder_used.label: Is extruder used?
is_extruder_used.tooltip: Vector of booleans stating whether a given extruder is used in the print.

is_imex.label: IDEX/IQEX Printer
is_imex.tooltip: Enable parallel printing for printers with multiple independent carriages (IDEX, IQEX, and similar).

is_infill_first.label: Print infill first
is_infill_first.tooltip:
Order of wall/infill. When the tickbox is unchecked the walls are printed first, which works best in most cases.

Printing infill first may help with extreme overhangs as the walls have the neighbouring infill to adhere to. However, the infill will slightly push out the printed walls where it is attached to them, resulting in a worse external surface finish. It can also cause the infill to shine through the external surfaces of the part.

last_extrusion_role.label: Last extrusion role
last_extrusion_role.tooltip:
The previously used extrusion role/type
Possible values:
["Perimeter", "ExternalPerimeter", "OverhangPerimeter", "InternalInfill", "SolidInfill", "TopSolidInfill", "BottomSurface", "BridgeInfill", "GapFill", "Ironing", "Skirt", "Brim", "SupportMaterial", "SupportMaterialInterface", "SupportTransition", "WipeTower", "Mixed"]

lateral_lattice_angle_1.label: Lateral lattice angle 1
lateral_lattice_angle_1.tooltip: The angle of the first set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

lateral_lattice_angle_2.label: Lateral lattice angle 2
lateral_lattice_angle_2.tooltip: The angle of the second set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

layer_change_gcode.label: Layer change G-code
layer_change_gcode.tooltip: This G-code is inserted at every layer change after the Z lift.

layer_height.label: Layer height
layer_height.tooltip: This is the height for each layer. Smaller layer heights give greater accuracy but longer printing time.

layer_num.label: Layer number
layer_num.tooltip: Index of the current layer. The index is zero-based (first layer has index 0). Before the first layer starts, it is -1. In extrusion role change G-code, the index is one-based (first layer has index 1).

layer_z.label: Layer Z
layer_z.tooltip: Height of the current layer above the print bed, measured to the top of the layer.

leading_brim_length.label: Leading brim length
leading_brim_length.tooltip:
Belt printers only. Extends the brim AHEAD of the object along the belt, on every downhill-facing edge of its contact area - both the object's first contact with the belt and any island that lands later. This apron is laid onto the belt before the object reaches it, so the leading edge has something already stuck down to hold on to.

Measured on the belt surface, and added on top of Brim width: the brim reaches Brim-object gap + Leading brim length + Brim width ahead of the object. Set Brim-object gap to 0, or the apron will not touch the object it is meant to anchor.

On a tilted belt each layer lays one strip of the brim, so the thickness of the resulting brim sheet is set by flow rather than by layer height. Use Brim flow ratio to tune it.

Set to 0 to disable.

lightning_overhang_angle.label: Lightning overhang angle
lightning_overhang_angle.tooltip: Maximum overhang angle for Lightning infill support propagation.

lightning_prune_angle.label: Prune angle
lightning_prune_angle.tooltip:
Controls how aggressively short or unsupported Lightning branches are pruned.
This angle is converted internally to a per-layer distance.

lightning_straightening_angle.label: Straightening angle
lightning_straightening_angle.tooltip: Maximum straightening angle used to simplify Lightning branches.

line_width.label: Default
line_width.tooltip: Default line width if other line widths are set to 0. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

load.label: Load config file
load.tooltip: Load configuration from the specified file. It can be used more than once to load options from multiple files.

load_assemble_list.label: Load assemble list
load_assemble_list.tooltip: Load assemble object list from config file.

load_defaultfila.label: Load default filaments
load_defaultfila.tooltip: Load first filament as default for those not loaded.

load_filament_ids.label: Load filament IDs
load_filament_ids.tooltip: Load filament IDs for each object.

load_filaments.label: Load Filament Settings
load_filaments.tooltip: Load filament settings from the specified file list.

load_settings.label: Load General Settings
load_settings.tooltip: Load process/machine settings from the specified file.

load_slicedata.label: Load slicing data
load_slicedata.tooltip: Load cached slicing data from directory.

long_retractions_when_cut.label: Long retraction when cut (beta)
long_retractions_when_cut.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retracting and cutting off the filament at a longer distance during changes to minimize purge. While this reduces flush significantly, it may also raise the risk of nozzle clogs or other printing problems.

machine_bed_mass_Y.tooltip: The machine bed mass load of Y axis
machine_bed_mass_Y.full_label: Bed mass of the Y axis

machine_end_gcode.label: End G-code
machine_end_gcode.tooltip: Add end G-code when finishing the entire print.
machine_end_gcode.default:
"M104 S0 ; turn off temperature
G28 X0  ; home X axis
M84     ; disable motors
"

machine_load_filament_time.label: Filament load time
machine_load_filament_time.tooltip: Time to load new filament when switch filament. It's usually applicable for single-extruder multi-material machines. For tool changers or multi-tool machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

machine_max_acceleration_travel.tooltip: Maximum acceleration for travel (M204 T), it only applies to Marlin 2.

machine_max_force_Y.tooltip: The allowed maximum output force of Y axis
machine_max_force_Y.full_label: Maximum force of the Y axis

machine_max_junction_deviation.tooltip:
Maximum junction deviation (M205 J, only apply if JD > 0 for Marlin Firmware
If your Marlin 2 printer uses Classic Jerk set this value to 0.)

machine_max_printed_mass.tooltip: The allowed max printed mass on a plate

machine_pause_gcode.label: Pause G-code
machine_pause_gcode.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a code for the pause print. Users can insert pause G-code in the G-code viewer.

machine_start_gcode.label: Start G-code
machine_start_gcode.tooltip: G-code added when starting a print.
machine_start_gcode.default: "G28 ; home all axes\nG1 Z5 F5000 ; lift nozzle\n"

machine_tool_change_time.label: Tool change time
machine_tool_change_time.tooltip: Time taken to switch tools. It's usually applicable for tool changers or multi-tool machines. For single-extruder multi-material machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

machine_unload_filament_time.label: Filament unload time
machine_unload_filament_time.tooltip: Time to unload old filament when switch filament. It's usually applicable for single-extruder multi-material machines. For tool changers or multi-tool machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

make_overhang_printable.label: Make overhangs printable
make_overhang_printable.tooltip: Modify the geometry to print overhangs without support material.

make_overhang_printable_angle.label: Make overhangs printable - Maximum angle
make_overhang_printable_angle.tooltip: Maximum angle of overhangs to allow after making more steep overhangs printable.90° will not change the model at all and allow any overhang, while 0 will replace all overhangs with conical material.

make_overhang_printable_hole_size.label: Make overhangs printable - Hole area
make_overhang_printable_hole_size.tooltip: Maximum area of a hole in the base of the model before it's filled by conical material. A value of 0 will fill all the holes in the model base.

manual_filament_change.label: Manual Filament Change
manual_filament_change.tooltip: Enable this option to omit the custom Change filament G-code only at the beginning of the print. The tool change command (e.g., T0) will be skipped throughout the entire print. This is useful for manual multi-material printing, where we use M600/PAUSE to trigger the manual filament change action.

master_extruder_id.label: Master extruder id
master_extruder_id.tooltip: Default extruder id to place filament.

max_bridge_length.label: Max bridge length
max_bridge_length.tooltip: This is the maximum length of bridges that don\'t need support. Set it to 0 if you want all bridges to be supported, and set it to a very large value if you don\'t want any bridges to be supported.

max_layer_height.label: Max
max_layer_height.tooltip: The highest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the maximum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.

max_layer_z.label: Maximal layer Z
max_layer_z.tooltip: Height of the last layer above the print bed.

max_travel_detour_distance.label: Avoid crossing walls - Max detour length
max_travel_detour_distance.tooltip: Maximum detour distance for avoiding crossing wall: The printer won\'t detour if the detour distance is larger than this value. Detour length could be specified either as an absolute value or as percentage (for example 50%) of a direct travel path. A value of 0 will disable this.

max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope.label: Extrusion rate smoothing
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope.tooltip:
This parameter smooths out sudden extrusion rate changes that happen when the printer transitions from printing a high flow (high speed/larger width) extrusion to a lower flow (lower speed/smaller width) extrusion and vice versa.

It defines the maximum rate by which the extruded volumetric flow in mm³/s can change over time. Higher values mean higher extrusion rate changes are allowed, resulting in faster speed transitions.

A value of 0 disables the feature.

For a high speed, high flow direct drive printer (like the Bambu lab or Voron) this value is usually not needed. However it can provide some marginal benefit in certain cases where feature speeds vary greatly. For example, when there are aggressive slowdowns due to overhangs. In these cases a high value of around 300-350 mm³/s² is recommended as this allows for just enough smoothing to assist pressure advance achieve a smoother flow transition.

For slower printers without pressure advance, the value should be set much lower. A value of 10-15 mm³/s² is a good starting point for direct drive extruders and 5-10 mm³/s² for Bowden style.

This feature is known as Pressure Equalizer in Prusa slicer.

Note: this parameter disables arc fitting.

max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_segm.label: Smoothing segment length
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_segm.tooltip:
A lower value results in smoother extrusion rate transitions. However, this results in a significantly larger G-code file and more instructions for the printer to process.

Default value of 3 works well for most cases. If your printer is stuttering, increase this value to reduce the number of adjustments made.

Allowed values: 0.5-5

min_bead_width.label: Minimum wall width
min_bead_width.tooltip: Width of the wall that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum feature size) of the model. If the Minimum wall width is thinner than the thickness of the feature, the wall will become as thick as the feature itself. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

min_feature_size.label: Minimum feature size
min_feature_size.tooltip: Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features that are thinner than this value will not be printed, while features thicker than than this value will be widened to the minimum wall width. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

min_layer_height.label: Min
min_layer_height.tooltip: The lowest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the minimum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.

min_length_factor.label: Minimum wall length
min_length_factor.tooltip:
Adjust this value to prevent short, unclosed walls from being printed, which could increase print time. The value is a multiple of the wall width. Higher values remove more and longer walls.

NOTE: Bottom and top surfaces will not be affected by this value to prevent visual gaps on the outside of the model. Adjust 'One wall threshold' in the 'Walls and surfaces' settings below to adjust the sensitivity of what is considered a top-surface. 'One wall threshold' is only visible if this setting is set above the default value of 0.5, or if single-wall top surfaces is enabled.

min_skirt_length.label: Skirt minimum extrusion length
min_skirt_length.tooltip:
Minimum filament extrusion length in mm when printing the skirt. Zero means this feature is disabled.

Using a non-zero value is useful if the printer is set up to print without a prime line.
Final number of loops is not taking into account while arranging or validating objects distance. Increase loop number in such case.

min_width_top_surface.label: One wall threshold
min_width_top_surface.tooltip:
If a top surface has to be printed and it's partially covered by another layer, it won't be considered at a top layer where its width is below this value. This can be useful to not let the 'one perimeter on top' trigger on surface that should be covered only by perimeters. This value can be a mm or a % of the perimeter extrusion width.

Warning: If enabled, artifacts can be created if you have some thin features on the next layer, like letters. Set this setting to 0 to remove these artifacts.

minimum_sparse_infill_area.label: Minimum sparse infill threshold
minimum_sparse_infill_area.tooltip: Sparse infill areas which are smaller than this threshold value are replaced by internal solid infill.

mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth.label: Interlocking depth of a segmented region
mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth.tooltip: Interlocking depth of a segmented region. On every other layer, the segmented region is limited to this depth. It will be ignored if "interlocking_beam" is enabled. Zero disables this feature.

mmu_segmented_region_max_width.label: Maximum width of a segmented region
mmu_segmented_region_max_width.tooltip: Maximum width of a segmented region. A value of 0 disables this feature.

mstpp.label: mstpp
mstpp.tooltip: max slicing time per plate in seconds

mtcpp.label: mtcpp
mtcpp.tooltip: max triangle count per plate for slicing

no_check.label: No check
no_check.tooltip: Do not run any validity checks, such as G-code path conflicts check.

normal_print_time.label: Print time (normal mode)
normal_print_time.tooltip: Estimated print time when printed in normal mode (i.e. not in silent mode). Same as print_time.

notes.label: Configuration notes
notes.tooltip: You can put here your personal notes. This text will be added to the G-code header comments.

nozzle_hrc.label: Nozzle HRC
nozzle_hrc.tooltip: The nozzle\'s hardness. Zero means no checking for nozzle hardness during slicing.

nozzle_temperature.label: Other layers
nozzle_temperature.tooltip: Nozzle temperature after the first layer

nozzle_temperature_initial_layer.label: First layer
nozzle_temperature_initial_layer.tooltip: Nozzle temperature for printing the first layer with this filament

nozzle_type.label: Nozzle type
nozzle_type.tooltip: The metallic material of the nozzle: This determines the abrasive resistance of the nozzle and what kind of filament can be printed.

nozzle_volume.label: Nozzle volume
nozzle_volume.tooltip: Volume of nozzle between the filament cutter and the end of the nozzle

num_extruders.label: Number of extruders
num_extruders.tooltip: Total number of extruders, regardless of whether they are used in the current print.

num_instances.label: Number of instances
num_instances.tooltip: Total number of object instances in the print, summed over all objects.

num_objects.label: Number of objects
num_objects.tooltip: Total number of objects in the print.

only_one_wall_first_layer.label: Only one wall on first layer
only_one_wall_first_layer.tooltip: Use only one wall on first layer, to give more space to the bottom infill pattern.

only_one_wall_top.label: Only one wall on top surfaces
only_one_wall_top.tooltip: Use only one wall on flat top surfaces, to give more space to the top infill pattern.

ooze_prevention.label: Enable
ooze_prevention.tooltip: This option will drop the temperature of the inactive extruders to prevent oozing.

other_layers_print_sequence_nums.label: The number of other layers print sequence

outer_wall_acceleration.label: Outer wall
outer_wall_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of outer wall: using a lower value can improve quality.

outer_wall_filament_id.label: Outer walls
outer_wall_filament_id.tooltip:
Filament to print outer walls.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

outer_wall_flow_ratio.label: Outer wall flow ratio
outer_wall_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for outer walls.

The actual outer wall flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

outer_wall_line_width.label: Outer wall
outer_wall_line_width.tooltip: Line width of outer wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

outer_wall_speed.label: Outer wall
outer_wall_speed.tooltip: This is the printing speed for the outer walls of parts. These are generally printed slower than inner walls for higher quality.

output.label: Output File
output.tooltip: The file where the output will be written (if not specified, it will be based on the input file).

outputdir.label: Output directory
outputdir.tooltip: This is the output directory for exported files.

overhang_fan_speed.label: Overhangs and external bridges fan speed
overhang_fan_speed.tooltip:
Use this part cooling fan speed when printing bridges or overhang walls with an overhang threshold that exceeds the value set in the 'Overhangs cooling threshold' parameter above. Increasing the cooling specifically for overhangs and bridges can improve the overall print quality of these features.

Please note, this fan speed is clamped on the lower end by the minimum fan speed threshold set above. It is also adjusted upwards up to the maximum fan speed threshold when the minimum layer time threshold is not met.

overhang_fan_threshold.label: Overhang cooling activation threshold
overhang_fan_threshold.tooltip: When the overhang exceeds this specified threshold, force the cooling fan to run at the 'Overhang Fan Speed' set below. This threshold is expressed as a percentage, indicating the portion of each line's width that is unsupported by the layer beneath it. Setting this value to 0% forces the cooling fan to run for all outer walls, regardless of the overhang degree.

overhang_flow_ratio.label: Overhang flow ratio
overhang_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for overhangs.

The actual overhang flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

overhang_reverse.label: Reverse on even
overhang_reverse.tooltip:
Extrude perimeters that have a part over an overhang in the reverse direction on even layers. This alternating pattern can drastically improve steep overhangs.

This setting can also help reduce part warping due to the reduction of stresses in the part walls.

overhang_reverse_internal_only.label: Reverse only internal perimeters
overhang_reverse_internal_only.tooltip:
Apply the reverse perimeters logic only on internal perimeters.

This setting greatly reduces part stresses as they are now distributed in alternating directions. This should reduce part warping while also maintaining external wall quality. This feature can be very useful for warp prone material, like ABS/ASA, and also for elastic filaments, like TPU and Silk PLA. It can also help reduce warping on floating regions over supports.

For this setting to be the most effective, it is recommended to set the Reverse Threshold to 0 so that all internal walls print in alternating directions on even layers irrespective of their overhang degree.

overhang_reverse_threshold.label: Reverse threshold
overhang_reverse_threshold.tooltip:
Number of mm the overhang need to be for the reversal to be considered useful. Can be a % of the perimeter width.
Value 0 enables reversal on every even layers regardless.
When Detect overhang wall is not enabled, this option is ignored and reversal happens on every even layers regardless.

parallel_printheads_bed_exclude_areas.label: Parallel printheads bed exclude areas
parallel_printheads_bed_exclude_areas.tooltip: Ordered list of bed exclude areas by parallel printhead count. Item 1 applies to one printhead, item 2 to two printheads, and so on. Leave an item empty for no excluded area.

parallel_printheads_count.label: Parallel printheads count
parallel_printheads_count.tooltip: Set the number of parallel printheads for machines like OrangeStorm Giga printer.

parking_pos_retraction.label: Filament parking position
parking_pos_retraction.tooltip: Distance of the extruder tip from the position where the filament is parked when unloaded. This should match the value in printer firmware.

part_cooling_fan_min_pwm.label: Minimum non-zero part cooling fan speed
part_cooling_fan_min_pwm.tooltip:
Some part-cooling fans cannot start spinning when commanded below a certain PWM duty cycle. When set above 0, any non-zero part-cooling fan command will be raised to at least this percentage so the fan reliably starts. A fan command of 0 (fan off) is always honoured exactly. This clamp is applied after every other fan calculation (first-layer ramp, layer-time interpolation, overhang/bridge/support-interface/ironing overrides), so scaling still operates within the range [this value, 100%].
If your firmware already disables the fan below a threshold (for example Klipper's [fan] off_below: 0.10 shuts the fan off whenever the commanded duty cycle is below 10%), this option and the firmware threshold should ideally be set to the same value. Matching them (e.g. off_below: 0.10 in Klipper and 10% here) guarantees the slicer never emits a non-zero value that the firmware would silently drop, and the fan never receives a value below the one you know it can actually spool at.
Set to 0 to deactivate.

pellet_flow_coefficient.label: Pellet flow coefficient
pellet_flow_coefficient.tooltip:
Pellet flow coefficient is empirically derived and allows for volume calculation for pellet printers.

Internally it is converted to filament_diameter. All other volume calculations remain the same.

filament_diameter = sqrt( (4 * pellet_flow_coefficient) / PI )

pellet_modded_printer.label: Pellet Modded Printer
pellet_modded_printer.tooltip: Enable this option if your printer uses pellets instead of filaments.

physical_extruder_map.label: Map the logical extruder to physical extruder
physical_extruder_map.tooltip: Map the logical extruder to physical extruder.

physical_printer_preset.label: Physical printer name
physical_printer_preset.tooltip: Name of the physical printer used for slicing.

plugins.label: Plugins Used
plugins.tooltip: Plugin capabilities referenced by this preset, stored as name;uuid;capability.

position.label: Position
position.tooltip: Position of the extruder at the beginning of the custom G-code block. If the custom G-code travels somewhere else, it should write to this variable so OrcaSlicer knows where it travels from when it gets control back.

post_process.label: Post-processing Scripts
post_process.tooltip: If you want to process the output G-code through custom scripts, just list their absolute paths here. Separate multiple scripts with a semicolon. Scripts will be passed the absolute path to the G-code file as the first argument, and they can access the Orca Slicer config settings by reading environment variables.

precise_outer_wall.label: Precise wall
precise_outer_wall.tooltip:
Improve shell precision by adjusting outer wall spacing. This also improves layer consistency.

Note: This option will be ignored for outer-inner or inner-outer-inner wall sequences.

precise_z_height.label: Precise Z height
precise_z_height.tooltip: Enable this to get precise Z height of object after slicing. It will get the precise object height by fine-tuning the layer heights of the last few layers. Note that this is an experimental parameter.

preferred_orientation.label: Preferred orientation
preferred_orientation.tooltip: Automatically orient STL files on the Z axis upon initial import.

preheat_steps.label: Preheat steps
preheat_steps.tooltip: Insert multiple preheat commands (e.g. M104.1). Only useful for Prusa XL. For other printers, please set it to 1.

preheat_time.label: Preheat time
preheat_time.tooltip: To reduce the waiting time after tool change, Orca can preheat the next tool while the current tool is still in use. This setting specifies the time in seconds to preheat the next tool. Orca will insert a M104 command to preheat the tool in advance.

pressure_advance.label: Pressure advance
pressure_advance.tooltip: Pressure advance (Klipper) AKA Linear advance factor (Marlin).

prime_tower_brim_width.label: Brim width
prime_tower_brim_width.tooltip: Brim width of prime tower, negative number means auto calculated width based on the height of prime tower.

prime_tower_enable_framework.label: Internal ribs
prime_tower_enable_framework.tooltip: Enable internal ribs to increase the stability of the prime tower.

prime_tower_skip_points.label: Skip points
prime_tower_skip_points.tooltip: The wall of prime tower will skip the start points of wipe path.

prime_tower_width.label: Width
prime_tower_width.tooltip: This is the width of prime towers.

prime_volume.label: Prime volume
prime_volume.tooltip: This is the volume of material to prime the extruder with on the tower.

prime_volume_mode.label: Prime volume mode
prime_volume_mode.tooltip: Selects how the wipe-tower prime and flush volumes are computed on multi-extruder printers.

print_bed_max.label: Top-right corner of print bed bounding box

print_bed_min.label: Bottom-left corner of print bed bounding box

print_bed_size.label: Size of the print bed bounding box

print_flow_ratio.label: Flow ratio
print_flow_ratio.tooltip:
The material may have volumetric change after switching between molten and crystalline states. This setting changes all extrusion flow of this filament in G-code proportionally. The recommended value range is between 0.95 and 1.05. You may be able to tune this value to get a nice flat surface if there is slight overflow or underflow.

The final object flow ratio is this value multiplied by the filament flow ratio.

print_host.label: Hostname, IP or URL
print_host.tooltip: Orca Slicer can upload G-code files to a printer host. This field should contain the hostname, IP address or URL of the printer host instance. Print host behind HAProxy with basic auth enabled can be accessed by putting the user name and password into the URL in the following format: https://username:password@your-octopi-address/

print_host_webui.label: Device UI
print_host_webui.tooltip: Specify the URL of your device user interface if it's not same as print_host.

print_order.label: Intra-layer order
print_order.tooltip:
Order in which object instances are visited within a single layer, which controls how much travel is spent moving between them.

Default: nearest-neighbor chaining, refined with 2-opt and crossing removal. A good general choice.
As object list: instances are printed in the same order as the object list, without any path optimization. Use it when you need a predictable, manually controlled order.
Best of all (shortest path): every strategy is evaluated and the shortest one is used. The object instance order is decided once for the whole print, while the ordering of individual islands is decided per layer, so different layers may end up using different strategies. Slightly slower to slice.
Snake: serpentine row-by-row traversal, refined with 2-opt. Well suited to regular grids of many small parts.

With multiple filaments or tools in the same layer, minimizing tool changes takes priority: objects are grouped by filament first and this setting only orders the instances within each filament group, so the overall sequence may not look like the shortest path across the plate.

print_preset.label: Print preset name
print_preset.tooltip: Name of the print preset used for slicing.

print_sequence.label: Print sequence
print_sequence.tooltip: This determines the print sequence, allowing you to print layer-by-layer or object-by-object.

print_time.label: Print time (normal mode)
print_time.tooltip: Estimated print time when printed in normal mode (i.e. not in silent mode). Same as normal_print_time.

print_time_day.label: Print time (days component)
print_time_day.tooltip: Estimated print time day component (normal mode). Replaced with actual value during post-processing.

print_time_hour.label: Print time (hours component)
print_time_hour.tooltip: Estimated print time hour component (normal mode). Replaced with actual value during post-processing.

print_time_minute.label: Print time (minutes component)
print_time_minute.tooltip: Estimated print time minute component (normal mode). Replaced with actual value during post-processing.

print_time_sec.label: Print time (seconds component)
print_time_sec.tooltip: Estimated print time second component (normal mode). Replaced with actual value during post-processing.

print_time_total_sec.label: Print time (total seconds)
print_time_total_sec.tooltip: Total estimated print time in seconds. Replaced with actual value during post-processing.

printable_height.label: Printable height
printable_height.tooltip: This is the maximum printable height which is limited by the height of the build area.

printer_agent.label: Printer Agent
printer_agent.tooltip: Select the network agent implementation for printer communication.

printer_notes.label: Printer notes
printer_notes.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the printer here.

printer_preset.label: Printer preset name
printer_preset.tooltip: Name of the printer preset used for slicing.

printer_structure.label: Printer structure
printer_structure.tooltip: The physical arrangement and components of a printing device.

printhost_apikey.label: API Key / Password
printhost_apikey.tooltip: Orca Slicer can upload G-code files to a printer host. This field should contain the API Key or the password required for authentication.

printhost_cafile.label: HTTPS CA File
printhost_cafile.tooltip: Custom CA certificate file can be specified for HTTPS OctoPrint connections, in crt/pem format. If left blank, the default OS CA certificate repository is used.

printhost_ssl_ignore_revoke.label: Ignore HTTPS certificate revocation checks
printhost_ssl_ignore_revoke.tooltip: Ignore HTTPS certificate revocation checks in the case of missing or offline distribution points. One may want to enable this option for self signed certificates if connection fails.

printing_by_object_gcode.label: Between Object G-code
printing_by_object_gcode.tooltip: Insert G-code between objects. This parameter will only come into effect when you print your models object by object.

process_change_extrusion_role_gcode.label: Change extrusion role G-code (process)
process_change_extrusion_role_gcode.tooltip: This G-code is inserted when the extrusion role is changed. It runs after the machine and filament extrusion role G-code.

purge_in_prime_tower.label: Purge in prime tower
purge_in_prime_tower.tooltip: Purge remaining filament into prime tower.

raft_contact_distance.label: Raft contact Z distance
raft_contact_distance.tooltip: Z gap between raft and object. If Support Top Z Distance is 0, this value is ignored and the object is printed in direct contact with the raft (no gap).

raft_expansion.label: Raft expansion
raft_expansion.tooltip: This expands all raft layers in XY plane.

raft_first_layer_density.label: First layer density
raft_first_layer_density.tooltip: This is the density of the first raft or support layer.

raft_first_layer_expansion.label: First layer expansion
raft_first_layer_expansion.tooltip: This expands the first raft or support layer to improve bed adhesion.

raft_layers.label: Raft layers
raft_layers.tooltip: Object will be raised by this number of support layers. Use this function to avoid warping when printing ABS.

reduce_crossing_wall.label: Avoid crossing walls
reduce_crossing_wall.tooltip: This detours to avoid traveling across walls, which may cause blobs on the surface.

reduce_fan_stop_start_freq.label: Keep fan always on
reduce_fan_stop_start_freq.tooltip: Enabling this setting means that part cooling fan will never stop entirely and will instead run at least at minimum speed to reduce the frequency of starting and stopping.

reduce_infill_retraction.label: Reduce infill retraction
reduce_infill_retraction.tooltip:
Don\'t retract when the travel is entirely within an infill area. That means the oozing can\'t been seen. This can reduce times of retraction for complex model and save printing time, but make slicing and G-code generating slower.

Note that Z-hop is also not performed in areas where retraction is skipped.

relative_bridge_angle.label: Relative bridge angle
relative_bridge_angle.tooltip: When enabled, the bridge angle values are added to the automatically calculated bridge direction instead of overriding it.

repair.label: Repair
repair.tooltip: Repair the meshes of the models as Fix Model does: close holes and cracks, orient them outward and remove self-intersections.

repetitions.label: Repetition count
repetitions.tooltip: Repetition count of the whole model.

required_nozzle_HRC.label: Required nozzle HRC
required_nozzle_HRC.tooltip: Minimum HRC of nozzle required to print the filament. A value of 0 means no checking of the nozzle\'s HRC.

resolution.label: Resolution
resolution.tooltip: The G-code path is generated after simplifying the contour of models to avoid too many points and G-code lines. Smaller values mean higher resolution and more time required to slice.

resonance_avoidance.label: Resonance avoidance
resonance_avoidance.tooltip:
By reducing the speed of the outer wall to avoid the resonance zone of the printer, ringing on the surface of the model are avoided.
Please turn this option off when testing ringing.

retract_after_wipe.label: Retract amount after wipe
retract_after_wipe.tooltip:
This is the length of fast retraction after wipe, relative to retraction length.
The value will be clamped by 100% minus the retract amount before the wipe value.

retract_before_wipe.label: Retract amount before wipe
retract_before_wipe.tooltip: This is the length of fast retraction before a wipe, relative to retraction length.

retract_length_toolchange.label: Retraction Length (Toolchange)
retract_length_toolchange.tooltip: When retraction is triggered before changing tool, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

retract_lift_above.label: Z-hop lower boundary
retract_lift_above.tooltip: Z-hop will only come into effect when Z is above this value and is below the parameter: "Z-hop upper boundary".

retract_lift_below.label: Z-hop upper boundary
retract_lift_below.tooltip: If this value is positive, Z-hop will only come into effect when Z is above the parameter: "Z-hop lower boundary" and is below this value.

retract_lift_enforce.label: On surfaces
retract_lift_enforce.tooltip: Enforce Z-Hop behavior. This setting is impacted by the above settings (Only lift Z above/below).

retract_restart_extra.label: Extra length on restart
retract_restart_extra.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

retract_restart_extra_toolchange.label: Extra length on restart (Toolchange)
retract_restart_extra_toolchange.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

retract_when_changing_layer.label: Retract on layer change
retract_when_changing_layer.tooltip: This forces a retraction on layer changes.

retraction_distances_when_cut.label: Retraction distance when cut
retraction_distances_when_cut.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retraction length before cutting off during filament change.

retraction_length.label: Length
retraction_length.tooltip: Some amount of material in extruder is pulled back to avoid ooze during long travel. Set zero to disable retraction.

retraction_minimum_travel.label: Travel distance threshold
retraction_minimum_travel.tooltip: Only trigger retraction when the travel distance is longer than this threshold.

retraction_speed.label: Retraction speed
retraction_speed.tooltip: Speed for retracting filament from the nozzle.

role_based_wipe_speed.label: Role based wipe speed
role_based_wipe_speed.tooltip: The wipe speed is determined by the speed of the current extrusion role. e.g. if a wipe action is executed immediately following an outer wall extrusion, the speed of the outer wall extrusion will be utilized for the wipe action.

rotate.label: Rotate
rotate.tooltip: Rotation angle around the Z axis in degrees.

rotate_x.label: Rotate around X
rotate_x.tooltip: Rotation angle around the X axis in degrees.

rotate_y.label: Rotate around Y
rotate_y.tooltip: Rotation angle around the Y axis in degrees.

scale.label: Scale
scale.tooltip: Scale the model by a float factor.

scale_to_fit.label: Scale to Fit
scale_to_fit.tooltip: Scale to fit the given volume.

scan_first_layer.label: Scan first layer
scan_first_layer.tooltip: Enable this to allow the camera on the printer to check the quality of the first layer.

scarf_angle_threshold.label: Conditional angle threshold
scarf_angle_threshold.tooltip:
This option sets the threshold angle for applying a conditional scarf joint seam.
If the maximum angle within the perimeter loop exceeds this value (indicating the absence of sharp corners), a scarf joint seam will be used. The default value is 155°.

scarf_joint_flow_ratio.label: Scarf joint flow ratio
scarf_joint_flow_ratio.tooltip: This factor affects the amount of material for scarf joints.

scarf_joint_speed.label: Scarf joint speed
scarf_joint_speed.tooltip:
This option sets the printing speed for scarf joints. It is recommended to print scarf joints at a slow speed (less than 100 mm/s). It's also advisable to enable 'Extrusion rate smoothing' if the set speed varies significantly from the speed of the outer or inner walls.

If the speed specified here is higher than the speed of the outer or inner walls, the printer will default to the slower of the two speeds. When specified as a percentage (e.g., 80%), the speed is calculated based on the respective outer or inner wall speed. The default value is set to 100%.

scarf_overhang_threshold.label: Conditional overhang threshold
scarf_overhang_threshold.tooltip: This option determines the overhang threshold for the application of scarf joint seams. If the unsupported portion of the perimeter is less than this threshold, scarf joint seams will be applied. The default threshold is set at 40% of the external wall's width. Due to performance considerations, the degree of overhang is estimated.

seam_gap.label: Seam gap
seam_gap.tooltip:
In order to reduce the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, the loop is interrupted and shortened by a specified amount.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the nozzle diameter. The default value for this parameter is 10%.

seam_position.label: Seam position
seam_position.tooltip: This is the starting position for each part of the outer wall.

seam_slope_conditional.label: Conditional scarf joint
seam_slope_conditional.tooltip: Apply scarf joints only to smooth perimeters where traditional seams do not conceal the seams at sharp corners effectively.

seam_slope_entire_loop.label: Scarf around entire wall
seam_slope_entire_loop.tooltip: The scarf extends to the entire length of the wall.

seam_slope_inner_walls.label: Scarf joint for inner walls
seam_slope_inner_walls.tooltip: Use scarf joint for inner walls as well.

seam_slope_min_length.label: Scarf length
seam_slope_min_length.tooltip: Length of the scarf. Setting this parameter to zero effectively disables the scarf.

seam_slope_start_height.label: Scarf start height
seam_slope_start_height.tooltip:
Start height of the scarf.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current layer height. The default value for this parameter is 0.

seam_slope_steps.label: Scarf steps
seam_slope_steps.tooltip: Minimum number of segments of each scarf.

seam_slope_type.label: Scarf joint seam (beta)
seam_slope_type.tooltip: Use scarf joint to minimize seam visibility and increase seam strength.

separated_infills.label: Separated infills
separated_infills.tooltip:
Centers the internal infill of each part on itself, as if it were sliced on its own, instead of on the whole assembly. Parts that touch or overlap are treated as one body and share a center; separate parts (or distinct 3D objects) each get their own.
Useful when an assembly groups several objects that should each keep a consistent, self-centered infill.
Adaptive Cubic and Support Cubic always center each part on itself, and Lightning infill is generated for the whole object and is unaffected.

set_other_flow_ratios.label: Set other flow ratios
set_other_flow_ratios.tooltip: Change flow ratios for other extrusion path types.

silent_mode.label: Supports silent mode
silent_mode.tooltip: Whether the machine supports silent mode in which machine use lower acceleration to print.

silent_print_time.label: Print time (silent mode)
silent_print_time.tooltip: Estimated print time when printed in silent mode.

single_extruder_multi_material.label: Single Extruder Multi Material
single_extruder_multi_material.tooltip: Use single nozzle to print multi filament.

single_extruder_multi_material_priming.label: Prime all printing extruders
single_extruder_multi_material_priming.tooltip: If enabled, all printing extruders will be primed at the front edge of the print bed at the start of the print.

single_instance.label: Single instance mode
single_instance.tooltip: If enabled, the command line arguments are sent to an existing instance of GUI OrcaSlicer, or an existing OrcaSlicer window is activated. Overrides the "single_instance" configuration value from application preferences.

single_loop_draft_shield.label: Single loop after first layer
single_loop_draft_shield.tooltip: Limits the skirt/draft shield loops to one wall after the first layer. This is useful, on occasion, to conserve filament but may cause the draft shield/skirt to warp / crack.

skeleton_infill_density.label: Skeleton infill density
skeleton_infill_density.tooltip: The remaining part of the model contour after removing a certain depth from the surface is called the skeleton. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skeleton densities, their skeleton areas will develop overlapping sections. Default is as same as infill density.

skeleton_infill_line_width.label: Skeleton line width
skeleton_infill_line_width.tooltip: Adjust the line width of the selected skeleton paths.

skin_infill_density.label: Skin infill density
skin_infill_density.tooltip: The portion of the model's outer surface within a certain depth range is called the skin. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skin densities, this area will not be split into two separate regions. Default is as same as infill density.

skin_infill_depth.label: Skin infill depth
skin_infill_depth.tooltip: The parameter sets the depth of skin.

skin_infill_line_width.label: Skin line width
skin_infill_line_width.tooltip: Adjust the line width of the selected skin paths.

skip_modified_gcodes.label: Skip modified G-code in 3MF
skip_modified_gcodes.tooltip: Skip the modified G-code in 3MF from printer or filament presets.

skip_objects.label: Skip Objects
skip_objects.tooltip: Skip some objects in this print.

skirt_distance.label: Skirt distance
skirt_distance.tooltip: This is the distance from the skirt to the brim or the object.

skirt_height.label: Skirt height
skirt_height.tooltip: Number of skirt layers: usually only one

skirt_loops.label: Skirt loops
skirt_loops.tooltip: This is the number of loops for the skirt. 0 means the skirt is disabled.

skirt_speed.label: Skirt speed
skirt_speed.tooltip: Speed of skirt, in mm/s. Zero means use default layer extrusion speed.

skirt_start_angle.label: Skirt start point
skirt_start_angle.tooltip: Angle from the object center to skirt start point. Zero is the most right position, counter clockwise is positive angle.

skirt_type.label: Skirt type
skirt_type.tooltip: Combined - single skirt for all objects, Per object - individual object skirt.

slice.label: Slice
slice.tooltip: Slice the plates: 0-all plates, i-plate i, others-invalid

slice_closing_radius.label: Slice gap closing radius
slice_closing_radius.tooltip: Cracks smaller than 2x gap closing radius are being filled during the triangle mesh slicing. The gap closing operation may reduce the final print resolution, therefore it is advisable to keep the value reasonably low.

slicing_mode.label: Slicing Mode
slicing_mode.tooltip: Use "Even-odd" for 3DLabPrint airplane models. Use "Close holes" to close all holes in the model.

slicing_pipeline_plugin.label: Slicing Pipeline Plugin
slicing_pipeline_plugin.tooltip: Python plugins invoked at each slicing pipeline step to read and modify intermediate slicing data, including a final G-code post-processing step. Research/experimental.

slow_down_for_layer_cooling.label: Slow printing down for better layer cooling
slow_down_for_layer_cooling.tooltip: Enable this option to slow printing speed down to ensure that the final layer time is not shorter than the layer time threshold in "Max fan speed threshold", so that the layer can be cooled for a longer time. This can improve the quality for small details.

slow_down_layer_time.label: Layer time
slow_down_layer_time.tooltip: The printing speed in exported G-code will be slowed down when the estimated layer time is shorter than this value in order to get better cooling for these layers.

slow_down_layers.label: Number of slow layers
slow_down_layers.tooltip: The first few layers are printed slower than normal. The speed is gradually increased in a linear fashion over the specified number of layers.

slow_down_min_speed.label: Min print speed
slow_down_min_speed.tooltip: The minimum print speed to which the printer slows down to maintain the minimum layer time defined above when the slowdown for better layer cooling is enabled.

slowdown_for_curled_perimeters.label: Slow down for curled perimeters
slowdown_for_curled_perimeters.tooltip:
Enable this option to slow down printing in areas where perimeters may have curled upwards.
For example, additional slowdown will be applied when printing overhangs on sharp corners like the front of the Benchy hull, reducing curling which compounds over multiple layers.

It is generally recommended to have this option switched on unless your printer cooling is powerful enough or the print speed is slow enough that perimeter curling does not happen.
If printing with a high external perimeter speed, this parameter may introduce wall artifacts when slowing down, due to the potentially large variance in print speeds causing the extruder to be unable to keep up with the requested flow change.
Root cause of these artifacts is most likely PA tuning being slightly off, especially when combined with a high PA smooth time.

Recommendations when enabling this option:
1. Reduce Pressure Advance smooth time to 0.015 - 0.02 so the extruder reacts quickly to the speed changes.
2. Increase the minimum print speeds to limit the magnitude of the slowdown and reduce the variance between fast and slow segments.
3. If artifacts still appear, enable Extrusion Rate Smoothing (ERS) to further smooth the flow transitions.

Note: When this option is enabled, overhang perimeters are treated like overhangs, meaning the overhang speed is applied even if the overhanging perimeter is part of a bridge.
For example, when the perimeters are 100% overhanging, with no wall supporting them from underneath, the 75% overhang speed will be applied, limited by the bridge speed.

small_area_infill_flow_compensation.label: Small area flow compensation (beta)
small_area_infill_flow_compensation.tooltip: Enable flow compensation for small infill areas.

small_area_infill_flow_compensation_mode.label: Flow Compensation Model
small_area_infill_flow_compensation_mode.tooltip: Flow Compensation Model, used to adjust the flow for small infill areas. The model is expressed as a comma separated pair of values for extrusion length and flow correction factor. Each pair is on a separate line, followed by a semicolon, in the following format: "1.234, 5.678;"

small_perimeter_speed.label: Small perimeters
small_perimeter_speed.tooltip: This separate setting will affect the speed of perimeters having radius <= small_perimeter_threshold (usually holes). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated on the outer wall speed setting above.

small_perimeter_threshold.label: Small perimeters threshold
small_perimeter_threshold.tooltip: This sets the threshold for small perimeter length. Default threshold is 0mm.

small_support_perimeter_speed.label: Small support perimeters
small_support_perimeter_speed.tooltip: Same as "Small perimeters", but for supports. This separate setting will affect the speed of support for areas <= `small_support_perimeter_threshold`. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 80%), it will be calculated on the support or support interface speed setting above.

small_support_perimeter_threshold.label: Small support perimeters threshold
small_support_perimeter_threshold.tooltip: This sets the threshold for small support perimeter length. The default threshold is 0mm.

solid_infill_direction.label: Solid infill direction
solid_infill_direction.tooltip: Angle for solid infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line.

solid_infill_rotate_template.label: Solid infill rotation template
solid_infill_rotate_template.tooltip:
This parameter adds a rotation of solid infill direction to each layer according to the specified template. The template is a comma-separated list of angles in degrees, e.g. '0,90'. The first angle is applied to the first layer, the second angle to the second layer, and so on. If there are more layers than angles, the angles will be repeated.

Note that not all solid infill patterns support rotation.

sparse_infill_acceleration.label: Sparse infill
sparse_infill_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of sparse infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.

sparse_infill_density.label: Sparse infill density
sparse_infill_density.tooltip: Density of internal sparse infill, 100% turns all sparse infill into solid infill and internal solid infill pattern will be used.

sparse_infill_filament_id.label: Infill
sparse_infill_filament_id.tooltip:
Filament to print internal sparse infill.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

sparse_infill_flow_ratio.label: Sparse infill flow ratio
sparse_infill_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for sparse infill.

The actual sparse infill flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

sparse_infill_line_width.label: Sparse infill
sparse_infill_line_width.tooltip: Line width of internal sparse infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

sparse_infill_pattern.label: Sparse infill pattern
sparse_infill_pattern.tooltip: This is the line pattern for internal sparse infill.

sparse_infill_rotate_template.label: Sparse infill rotation template
sparse_infill_rotate_template.tooltip:
Rotate the sparse infill direction per layer using a template of angles. Enter comma-separated degrees (e.g., '0,30,60,90'). Angles are applied in order by layer and repeat when the list ends.

Advanced syntax is supported: '+5' rotates +5° every layer; '+5#5' rotates +5° every 5 layers. See the Wiki for details.

When a template is set, the standard infill direction setting is ignored.

Note: some infill patterns (e.g., Gyroid) control rotation themselves; use with care.

sparse_infill_smooth_factor.label: Sparse infill smooth factor
sparse_infill_smooth_factor.tooltip: Controls how strongly sparse infill corners are rounded. 0% keeps the original sharp path, while 100% produces the largest possible curves between adjacent infill lines.

sparse_infill_speed.label: Sparse infill
sparse_infill_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for internal sparse infill.

spiral_finishing_flow_ratio.label: Spiral finishing flow ratio
spiral_finishing_flow_ratio.tooltip: Sets the finishing flow ratio while ending the spiral. Normally the spiral transition scales the flow ratio from 100% to 0% during the last loop which can in some cases lead to under extrusion at the end of the spiral.

spiral_mode.label: Spiral vase
spiral_mode.tooltip: This enables spiraling, which smooths out the Z moves of the outer contour and turns a solid model into a single walled print with solid bottom layers. The final generated model has no seam.

spiral_mode_max_xy_smoothing.label: Max XY Smoothing
spiral_mode_max_xy_smoothing.tooltip: Maximum distance to move points in XY to try to achieve a smooth spiral. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

spiral_mode_smooth.label: Smooth Spiral
spiral_mode_smooth.tooltip: Smooth Spiral smooths out X and Y moves as well, resulting in no visible seam at all, even in the XY directions on walls that are not vertical.

spiral_starting_flow_ratio.label: Spiral starting flow ratio
spiral_starting_flow_ratio.tooltip: Sets the starting flow ratio while transitioning from the last bottom layer to the spiral. Normally the spiral transition scales the flow ratio from 0% to 100% during the first loop which can in some cases lead to under extrusion at the start of the spiral.

split.label: Split
split.tooltip: Detect unconnected parts in the given models and split them into separate objects.

staggered_inner_seams.label: Staggered inner seams
staggered_inner_seams.tooltip: This option causes the inner seams to be shifted backwards based on their depth, forming a zigzag pattern.

standby_temperature_delta.label: Temperature variation
standby_temperature_delta.tooltip: Temperature difference to be applied when an extruder is not active. The value is not used when 'idle_temperature' in filament settings is set to non-zero value.

start_end_points.label: Start end points
start_end_points.tooltip: The start and end points which are from the cutter area to the excess chute.

strict.label: Strict mode
strict.tooltip: Exit non-zero when slicing raises a non-critical warning that is otherwise only logged, such as a model that needs support while support is disabled. Use this in CI or scripted pipelines that should never ship a subtly broken slice. Each such warning is also listed with a stable class in the `warnings` array of result.json, which is written on Linux only. Cannot be combined with --no-check, which skips the support check.

supertack_plate_temp.label: Other layers
supertack_plate_temp.tooltip: This is the bed temperature for layers except for the first one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate SuperTack.

supertack_plate_temp_initial_layer.label: First layer
supertack_plate_temp_initial_layer.tooltip: This is the bed temperature of the first layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate SuperTack.

support_air_filtration.label: Support air filtration
support_air_filtration.tooltip:
Enable this if the printer supports air filtration
G-code command: M106 P3 S(0-255)

support_angle.label: Pattern angle
